parsed.note: William James (1907) never mentioned '10 percent' or brain anatomy; he made a qualitative remark about untapped mental/physical potential, which Lowell Thomas (1936) falsely sharpened into the precise figure '10 percent of his latent mental ability' and falsely attributed the exact phrasing to James, then popular culture further mutated 'latent mental ability' into 'brain.'

chain.title: Introduction: 'A Shortcut to Distinction' by Lowell Thomas | How To Win Friends And Influence People
chain.exact_wording: Professor William James of Harvard used to say that the average man develops only 10 percent of his latent mental ability.
chain.change: Thomas introduced the specific '10 percent' figure and attributed it to William James; James's actual writings contain no such percentage or brain reference — this is the fabrication point

chain.title: Ten-percent-of-the-brain myth - Wikipedia
chain.exact_wording: Professor William James of Harvard used to say that the average man develops only ten percent of his latent mental ability
chain.change: Wikipedia correctly notes this quote appears in Thomas's 1936 foreword and is a falsely precise attribution; popular culture later shifted 'latent mental ability' to 'brain'

chain.title: Classics in the History of Psychology -- James (1907)
chain.exact_wording: Compared with what we ought to be, we are only half awake. We are making use of only a small part of our possible mental and physical resources.
chain.change: James's actual text: purely qualitative, no percentage, no mention of brain anatomy — the '10 percent' and 'brain' framings are entirely absent

chain.title: The Energies of Men - Wikisource, the free online library
chain.exact_wording: as a rule men habitually use only a small part of the powers which they actually possess and which they might use under appropriate conditions
chain.change: Corroborates the York University transcript: no percentage, no brain reference; James spoke of 'powers' and 'reserves of energy,' not neuroanatomy

searched_but_not_found: https://archive.org/details/energiesofmen00jameuoft — Internet Archive page for the 1914 Moffat Yard edition: metadata only, no body text, no '10 percent' claim

https://people.duke.edu/~tkb13/courses/ece458-2018sp/readings/How%20to%20Win%20Friends%20And%20Influence%20People.html — Duke-hosted HTML of Carnegie book: contains Carnegie's James quotation ('only half awake') but Lowell Thomas preface with '10 percent' is not present in this version
Albert Einstein Archives — no record found of Einstein attributing his intellect to using more than 10 percent of his brain

Any pre-1936 primary source containing the exact phrase '10 percent of the brain' — none found; the 1929 World Almanac ad used '10 percent of our brain power' in a self-help advertisement context, predating Thomas but still not traceable to a scientific study or interview
